desc:
Find every way to choose exactly k different digits from 1..9 so that they add up to n. Each digit can be used at most once in a combination.

Write every combination in strictly increasing order (for example [1,2,4], never [2,1,4]) and list every combination once. Rows may be returned in any order. If no combination exists, return an empty array.
hints: Build a combination digit by digit, remembering how many digits are still needed and how much sum is still missing.
Only allow digits bigger than the previous one, then every set is produced exactly once and already sorted.
Cut a branch when the missing sum is negative, or when the smallest possible way to finish (next digits d, d+1, ...) already exceeds it, or when too few digits remain to supply k more.
editorial: Recurse on (next_digit, digits_left, sum_left) with the chosen digits in a list. If digits_left == 0, record the list when sum_left == 0. Otherwise try each digit d from next_digit to 9 and recurse with d + 1, one digit fewer needed and sum_left - d. Because digits only increase along a path, every set of digits is visited once, in sorted order.

Pruning keeps it fast: once d > sum_left every later digit overshoots as well, so stop the loop. The whole search space is at most C(9, k) ≤ 126 leaves, so the running time is tiny; the point of the exercise is the clean start-index pattern used by all combination problems.
